[168] The passage explicitly states, "Thus, the Thirty Years' War would be the last war to be labeled a religious war." Therefore, the Thirty Years' War is described as the last 'religious war'.

[169] The passage states the mob forced the carriage windows open (A), forced an exit from Versailles (B), and forced a trip back to Paris (D). It mentions a member waved the head in front of the Queen, but does not state they were forced to view the actual beheading of a guard, only the displayed head (C).

[170] The passage states that the blockade caused "danger to even neutral ships." Option D claims it "ensured that neutral ships wouldn't be jeopardized," which contradicts the passage.

[171] The passage instructs to "ensure your safety" before checking a victim because getting hurt makes matters worse. Option A suggests not being concerned with sustaining own injuries, which contradicts this safety instruction.

[172] The passage states, "Almost everyone complains about transportation systems." This supports the statement in Option C that they cause a lot of complaints.

[173] The passage states effects depend on "type of mutation," "significance of the piece," and "whether the cells... are germ-line." It does not list the quantity ("how much") of genetic material as a factor.

[174] Options A, B, and C are contradicted by the text regarding the majority (which are characteristics of the "most violent two percent" or generally false). The passage generalizes that "Tornadoes uproot trees," making Option D accurate for the category despite the stats on duration/speed being specific to the minor majority.

[175] The passage explains that iron tracks caused "more wear on the wooden wheels," leading to their eventual replacement by iron wheels. Option D accurately reflects this cause and effect.
